item.title: Re: Autonomous mapping bots and/or umbilicals? Or what about ground penetrating radar or some other sensors?
item.content:encoded:
If electronics are an issue; a clockwork automaton with simple analog sensors, that records its findings in punchcards, or grooves in vinyl records, or paper etc, could be used in place of a regular robot with electronic storage media.

Though, I interpreted the stuff about GPS, cellphones and remote control as just meaning that signals get absorbed by the walls, or maybe the atmosphere; and not that the electronics themselves fail. But considering that cameras and radio communications can get far inside, it seems the deterioration of signals is very reduced when the source/target of the signals is near the entrance (satellites and cell antennas are likely quite far away), which suggests remote control, if the control station antenna is close to the entrance, might allow for a bigger range (perhaps it's a matter of the frequencies used?).

And even if there is deterioration of signal based on distance for all signals, they could have the robot drop radio repeaters along the way

item.title: Re: Autonomous mapping bots and/or umbilicals? Or what about ground penetrating radar or some other sensors?
item.content:encoded:
GPS units used within SCP-432 are rendered useless, as are cellular phones. Remote-controlled devices sent into SCP-432 are similarly impaired and cease to function after travelling an average of 20 meters into the maze, rendering remote mapping of the internal layout impossible. High-gain radio transmissions can be used to keep in contact with personnel within the labyrinth, although significant interference occurs deeper into the maze.

Presumably autonomous robots and radar would have the same problems with massive interference (even an autonomous robot is going to have problems with induced EMF). If you could get anything useful out of a radar system, it might also set off the same "cheating senses" that cutting through the wall did. The problem with the umbilical is that they lead out as well as in- and there is something in that you really don't want to lead out.

I've been summoned back to this site by some recent fiction based on my first and only successful SCP!

I've decided to dish the truth of SCP-432, so listen up!

The cabinet and maze within is intended to be the legendary Labyrinth of Knossos. The monster is actually the Minotaur. The cabinet and the labyrinth within reshape themselves based on their surroundings; it currently looks like rusted metal and old pipes because it was left in an industrial building for a few decades.

After a little time in the SCP Foundation, it will start to reshape itself again…

item.content:encoded: I think that this SCP really just needs… something. Either something that makes it a threat, or something that would make it worth the foundation's while to send explorations in and risk getting people killed/wasting D-class subjects. For example, SCP-093 is fairly similar in concept (in the sense that it's a thingy that sends you to another dimension/universe/whatever), and it's obviously a formerly inhabited world that had succumbed to something or other. Understanding and stopping civilization destroying phenomena is the Foundation's MO, so obviously they're going to send investigative crews in for that. But for this… I don't know, to me it just sort of seems like they would've stopped after the animal attacked and just sorta locked it up. I kind of would like to see some sort of twist that made it obvious there was value to sending expeditions in there. Does that make sense? After that I'll give it a +1.

item.content:encoded:
Honestly, this seems like it'd probably translate well into a first-person maze-based RPG game, in the style of Wizardry or Etrian Odyssey. Generate an excessively large three dimensional maze at startup, place a number of roaming monsters about it, then put together a team of personnel to explore it. Each time you enter the maze, you enter at a different location, and can only exit at the point of entrance, enforcing mapping or even using the means used in the logs.

Only thing it's missing is the goal. The end point, if there ever would be one. If there isn't one, it could just be turned into a casual creep-factor game, what with the potential of hearing the noise from previous explorers lost in the maze, the monsters, etc.
